# Node Modules LLMs Server

## Overview

The Node Modules LLMs Server is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server designed to provide access to `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` files from npm packages located in `node_modules`. 
It enables dynamic resource handling and tool execution for interacting with these files.  
When installed, this allows AI agents to effectively consume documentation from our internal libraries and use that documentation to generate code and configs that propery use the libraries.

## Features

- **Resource Handling**: 
  - Exposes resource templates for `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` files.
  - Reads the content of `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` files from npm packages in `node_modules`.
  - Supports recursive search in subdirectories for `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` files.
  - Works with package names with optional prefixes (`@ps-refarch/`, `@ps-refarch-ux/`, `@powerschool-refarch/` and `@powerschool-refarch-ux/`).

- **Tool Execution**:
  Provides the following tools:
  - `discover_packages` to list out all the `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` files found in `node_modules`
  - `get_llms_file` to fetch the content of `llms.txt` files from a specified npm package.
  - `list_package_components` to return any inventory of components present in an `llms-full.txt` file
  - `get_component_details` to return the documentation in an `llms-full.txt` file for a specific component

- **Error Handling**:
  - Logs errors to the console.
  - Gracefully shuts down the server on `SIGINT` signal.

## Requirements

- Node.js
- MCP-compatible client (github copilot, roo code, etc.)

## Installation

Install the package from the PowerSchool Reference Architecture registry:

```bash
npm install @powerschool-refarch/node-modules-llms-server
```

## Configuration

To configure your MCP server to use the Node Modules LLMs Server, run:

```bash
npx node-modules-llms-help
```

This will output the configuration block that you should add to your MCP configuration file.

### Environment Variables

- **CWD**: Set this environment variable to specify the starting directory for searching packages. If not provided, the current working directory will be used.  Note that you MUST do this for github copilot as it does not set the CWD correctly on its own.

  Example:
  ```json
  "node-modules-llms": {
    "command": "node",
    "args": [
      "./node_modules/@powerschool-refarch/node-modules-llms-server/build/index.js"
    ],
    "env": {
      "CWD": "/path/to/project/root"
    },
    "disabled": false,
    "timeout": 60,
    "alwaysAllow": [
      "discover_packages",
      "get_llms_file",
      "list_package_components",
      "get_component_details"
    ]
  }
  ```

## Prompting and using with copilot/roo/etc.

Once installed and configured, you can refer to this server and the tools and resources it provides when prompting your agentic coding tools.  Here are some examples:

```
> Use the discover_packages tool and let me know which libraries have documentation available
```

If you have llms-full.txt files you can use the list_package_components and get_component_details tools in order to target the agent with just the needed docs
```
> Mock up a new react page using neon components that will support basic todo list functionality.  Use the list_package_components tool for @ps-refarch-ux/neon in order to find out what neon components exist.
```

```
> Use get_component_details to find all the correct props to use with NeonButton and fix the usage in my page.tsx file
```

For llms.txt files, you can have the agent pull the entire file to look up info
```
> I want to utilize the dispatchMfeEvent function in @ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils.  Use get_llms_file to get the documentation for this library and then update my code to correctly use this function.
```

If you have other MCPs, like a figma mcp, you can ask for multiple to be used
```
> I have a figma design here https://www.figma.com/design/a0P6Hj6INdTLTDH13Kvzm5/LOR---Simplified?node-id=382-25106&t=V6sGuo3Ng3ICp6f0-4  can you analyze it with the get_figma_data tool and create a plan for mocking it up using react neon components?  Use the node-modules-llms-help tools to find out all the documentation for @ps-refarch-ux/neon.  Pay special attention to the components and make sure you are using the right components, and laying them out correctly
```

### System prompts

If you want to avoid having to call out the tools all the time, you can update the System Prompt / custom instruction in your agent's config, for example put this in place
```
Use the node-modules-llms-help tools whenever you need to know info about the neon library, which is installed in @ps-refarch-ux/neon.

Use the get_figma_data tool whenever you have a url to a figma page and need to analyze it.
```

Then your prompt can be more like this
```
> I have a figma design here https://www.figma.com/design/a0P6Hj6INdTLTDH13Kvzm5/LOR---Simplified?node-id=382-25106&t=V6sGuo3Ng3ICp6f0-4  can you analyze it and create a plan for mocking it up using react neon components?  Pay special attention to the components and make sure you are using the right components, and laying them out correctly
```

Sometimes you may still need to refine what the agent has done by pointing it back to the tools
```
> Make sure to use the node-modules-llms-help get_component_details tool for each component to ensure you are using the neon components correctly.  Also pay careful attention to the layout to ensure the result will look similar to the figma mock
```


## How It Works

1. **Resource Templates**:
   - The server exposes a resource template with the URI format `llms://{packageName}`.
   - This template allows clients to request the content of `llms.txt` files for specific npm packages.

2. **Tool Handlers**:
   - The `discover_packages` tool takes no arguments and returns a list of all `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` files found.
   - The `get_llms_file` tool accepts a `packageName` as input and returns the content of the corresponding `llms.txt` file.
   - The `list_package_components` tool accepts a `packageName` as input and returns any list of components found in an `llms-full.txt` file for the package.
   - The `get_component_details` tool accepts a `packageName` and a `componentName` as input and returns the full details for the component found in the `llms-full.txt` file for the package.


3. **File Search**:
   - The server first checks the main `node_modules` directory for the `llms.txt` file.
   - If not found, it recursively searches subdirectories for the file.
   - It also tries different package name prefixes (`@ps-refarch/`, `@ps-refarch-ux/`, `@powerschool-refarch/` and `@powerschool-refarch-ux/`).


## Development Usage

1. Start the server by running the following command:
   ```bash
   # Using default current working directory
   node node_modules/@powerschool-refarch/node-modules-llms-server/build/index.js
   
   # Specifying a custom starting directory
   CWD=/path/to/project/root node node_modules/@powerschool-refarch/node-modules-llms-server/build/index.js
   ```

2. You can test it directly after npm install using the MCP inspector:
    ```bash
    npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node ./node_modules/@powerschool-refarch/node-modules-llms-server/build/index.js
    ```

### To publish new versions

Currently version numbering is manually maintained. To publish a new version:

1. Update the version number in package.json using semver-esque numbering
2. Commit and push
3. Pipeline will publish new version.

Tip: If you get a 403 error in the pipeline, you probably didn't update the package.json version.
